name: No-Knead Pot Bread
why: You asked about bread and you own everything for it: 2.5 kg of flour, instant yeast, and an oven-safe pot with a lid. No kneading and no skill required, only patience.

time.note: 15 min of work, 14 h of waiting

steps.text: In a big bowl mix 3 cups flour, 1/4 tsp instant yeast and 1.5 tsp kosher salt with a spoon.
steps.look: A quarter teaspoon of yeast for a whole loaf looks like a mistake and is not. The dough rises for 12 to 18 hours, so it needs almost none. More yeast here makes it rise too fast and taste of beer.

steps.text: Add 1.5 cups of room-temperature water and stir until there is no dry flour left. About 30 seconds.
steps.look: It will look shaggy, sticky and wrong, like a lumpy paste rather than a dough. That is exactly right. Do not knead it, do not add flour to fix it, do not tidy it up. The long rest does the work that kneading would.
steps.warn: Cold water slows the rise, hot water kills the yeast. Room temperature, straight from the tap.

steps.text: Cover the bowl with your second bowl upside down. Leave it on the counter 12 to 18 hours. Overnight is ideal.
steps.look: Done when the surface is covered in bubbles and it has roughly doubled. It should look wet, loose and alive.You have no plastic wrap and do not need any: an inverted bowl traps the moisture perfectly well.

steps.text: Tip the dough onto a floured counter. Fold it over on itself 4 times, turning a quarter each time, then flip it seam-side down.
steps.look: Flour your hands first, it is very sticky. This is 30 seconds of work, not kneading. You are just building enough surface tension for it to hold a round shape.

steps.text: Put it on a sheet of parchment, cover with the bowl again, rest 1 hour. In the last 30 minutes, put the empty pot with its lid on into the oven and heat to 450°F (230°C).
steps.look: Preheating the empty pot is the whole trick of this method. Dough hitting screaming-hot cast metal springs upward instead of spreading out.
steps.warn: That pot and lid come out at 450°F and look exactly like a cold pot. Oven mitts on before you touch anything, and put the lid somewhere it cannot be picked up absent-mindedly.

steps.text: Take the pot out, lift the lid, and lower the dough in on its parchment. Lid back on. 30 minutes.
steps.look: The parchment is your handle and it stays in with the bread. Never reach into the pot.The lid traps the doughâ€™s own steam, which is what makes a proper crust. This is a home oven imitating a steam-injected bakery oven, and it genuinely works.

steps.text: Lid off. Another 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden brown.
steps.look: Go darker than feels comfortable. Pale bread is underbaked bread, and the crust is where the flavour is.Done at 205°F inside on the thermometer. Without it: tip the loaf out and knock the base with a knuckle. A hollow sound means done, a dull thud means it needs longer.

steps.text: Cool on a rack, or propped against something, for at least 1 hour before cutting.
steps.look: The inside is still cooking as it cools. Cut it hot and the crumb collapses into something gummy. This is the hardest step and it is the one people skip.About 4 g of protein per slice. Bread is not a protein food here, it is a vehicle for the roast beef.
